newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu sees peace with Syria within four years.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu sees peace with Syria within four years.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Wednesday he was likely to make peace with Syria during his four-year term in office despite his refusal to return the Golan Heights, as Damascus is demanding.
Asked in an interview broadcast on CNN television if he thought an agreement was possible during his current four-year term, the Israeli leader, elected in May, said: "Yes."
"I think that it's a question of formula, of the right diplomatic work, (I think) that we will be at the negotiating table sooner or later."
He did not say how the two sides would resolve their land dispute.

Tensions between Israel and Syria have risen since Netanyahu was elected on a platform rejecting the land-for-peace formula that has been the linchpin of Middle East peace talks since 1991. Syria wants back all of the Golan Heights.

Its negotiators failed to strike an agreement with Israel's previous Labour government, which was ready to withdraw troops from at least part of the heights, something Netanyahu has said he will never do.
Guidelines for Netanyahu's government say: "Preserving Israeli sovereignty over the Golan will be the basis for any agreement with Syria."

Israel captured the Golan in the 1967 Middle East war and annexed it in 1981, deeming it essential for security. Sporadic peace talks launched a decade later have been suspended since February with Syria rejecting Israeli proposals for renewing the talks.
"Syria cannot and should not want to sustain a belligerent posture vis-a-vis Israel. It is not to its benefit and certainly it is our desire to make peace with Syria," Netanyahu said.
Israelis became war wary in September when Syria moved thousands of its troops in Lebanon towards the Israeli border and launched a series of offensive military exercises.
